items.title: Earl Turbinton Interview, 1990-09-01
items.q: I stayed in New York for a period of time with wonderful hospitality given to me by Walter Booker

ctx.x: the things that were money generating things that would have kept the place afloat and but it was a very warm and i'll never forget the loving uh atmosphere that was there and how these various cross sections of people came together uh another thing that's very that was uh very interesting that happened as a result of the workshop is that one of the groups of people that understood what we were going through possibly as much or more than anybody else was john o'neill and the people at the free southern theater…

which was half of the group at that time. And it was a long time. I mean, many, many years before I ever played with anybody that gave me the completeness and the fullness of playing with that particular group. In fact, we've never ever had that same setting together again. There have been times when it's been George French, David Lee, Willie T, and myself, or Willie T, David Lee, myself, or Willie T, Joyce Davis, and myself, but not all four of us back together again. As I said before, George French came as…

Can you address a little bit about what do you think the forces were that led to the closure? I mean, I know you said there were lots of other problems, but were there any other things that you think led to the closure?
